items.followUp: State four differences between plant and animal cells.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the nuclear organisation of the two cell types.
rubric.description: Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound nucleus; eukaryotes have a true nucleus.
rubric.how: Award for stating this contrast.

rubric.why: Identifies whether membrane-bound organelles are present.
rubric.description: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotes have them.
rubric.how: Award for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: States a key difference in chromosome form.
rubric.description: Prokaryotic DNA is usually circular; eukaryotic nuclear DNA is linear.
rubric.how: Award for stating both forms correctly.

rubric.why: Distinguishes their relative size and complexity.
rubric.description: Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and simpler; eukaryotic cells are generally larger and more complex.
rubric.how: Award for the correct comparison.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotic cells have no membrane-bound nucleus; their DNA lies in a nucleoid, whereas eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells contain them.
Prokaryotic DNA is usually circular and naked; eukaryotic nuclear DNA is linear and associated with proteins.
Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and simpler; eukaryotic cells are generally larger and more complex.

rubric.why: Identifies enzymes as biological catalysts.
rubric.description: Enzymes are biological catalysts.
rubric.how: Award for the correct defining characteristic.

rubric.why: Explains how enzymes affect reactions.
rubric.description: They lower activation energy and increase the rate of reactions.
rubric.how: Award for stating that they speed reactions by lowering activation energy.

rubric.why: Recognises the specificity of enzyme action.
rubric.description: Each enzyme acts on a particular substrate or type of reaction.
rubric.how: Award for correct substrate specificity.

rubric.why: States that enzymes remain available after catalysis.
rubric.description: Enzymes are not consumed in reactions and can be reused.
rubric.how: Award for stating that they remain unchanged or reusable.

rubric.why: Recognises that enzyme activity depends on conditions.
rubric.description: Enzymes work best at an optimum temperature and pH; extremes can denature them.
rubric.how: Award for a correct statement about optimum conditions or denaturation.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts, mostly made of proteins.
They lower the activation energy and increase the rate of biochemical reactions.
Each enzyme is specific for a particular substrate or reaction.
Enzymes are not used up during reactions and can be reused.
Each enzyme has an optimum temperature and pH; unsuitable conditions may denature it.

items.followUp: What is aerobic respiration? Briefly describe how it differs from anaerobic respiration.

rubric.why: Defines anaerobic respiration by its oxygen requirement and substrate.
rubric.description: Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose without oxygen.
rubric.how: Award for the definition.

rubric.why: States a general consequence of anaerobic breakdown.
rubric.description: Glucose is incompletely broken down and less energy is released than in aerobic respiration.
rubric.how: Award for incomplete breakdown or less energy.

rubric.why: Identifies the alcoholic type and its products or organism.
rubric.description: Alcoholic fermentation, occurring in yeast, produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Award for the correct type with products or yeast.

rubric.why: Identifies the lactic acid type and its product or occurrence.
rubric.description: Lactic acid fermentation produces lactic acid, for example in muscle cells or some bacteria.
rubric.how: Award for the correct type with its product or occurrence.

modelAnswer: Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose without oxygen.
It is an incomplete breakdown and releases less energy than aerobic respiration.
In alcoholic fermentation, yeast converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.
In lactic acid fermentation, glucose is broken down to lactic acid, as in muscle cells or some bacteria.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and functions of the small intestine.

rubric.why: Describes the stomach's general form and position.
rubric.description: The stomach is a J-shaped muscular sac in the upper abdomen, mainly on the left side.
rubric.how: Award for its shape and position or a clear equivalent.

rubric.why: Identifies the stomach's connections.
rubric.description: It receives food from the oesophagus and opens into the duodenum; sphincters regulate passage.
rubric.how: Award for naming both connections or the controlled passage.

rubric.why: Names important gastric secretions.
rubric.description: Gastric glands produce hydrochloric acid, pepsin and protective mucus.
rubric.how: Award for naming the secretions, including acid and pepsin.

rubric.why: Explains the stomach's mechanical role.
rubric.description: Muscular contractions churn and mix food with gastric juice, forming chyme.
rubric.how: Award for churning/mixing food or formation of chyme.

rubric.why: States an important function of the stomach.
rubric.description: The stomach begins protein digestion, helps kill microbes, and temporarily stores food.
rubric.how: Award for a correct function linked to a relevant secretion where applicable.

modelAnswer: The stomach is a J-shaped muscular sac situated in the upper abdomen, mainly on the left side.
It receives food from the oesophagus and opens into the duodenum; sphincters regulate the passage of food.
Gastric glands in its wall secrete gastric juice containing hydrochloric acid, pepsin and protective mucus.
The muscular walls churn and mix food with gastric juice, forming semi-liquid chyme.
Pepsin begins protein digestion, hydrochloric acid provides an acidic medium and helps kill bacteria, and the stomach temporarily stores food.

items.followUp: Describe the composition and functions of blood cells.

rubric.why: Describes the appearance and nature of plasma.
rubric.description: Plasma is the straw-coloured liquid part of blood.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as the liquid, straw-coloured component.

rubric.why: Gives the major component of plasma.
rubric.description: Plasma is mostly water, about 90–92%.
rubric.how: Award for water being the major component or the approximate proportion.

rubric.why: Names important plasma proteins.
rubric.description: Its proteins include albumin, globulins and fibrinogen.
rubric.how: Award for naming at least two plasma proteins or identifying plasma proteins with an example.

rubric.why: States the transport or clotting role of plasma.
rubric.description: Plasma transports dissolved substances and its fibrinogen contributes to blood clotting.
rubric.how: Award for a correct transport role or the clotting role of fibrinogen.

modelAnswer: Blood plasma is the straw-coloured liquid part of blood.
It consists mainly of water, about 90–92%, with dissolved substances.
Its proteins include albumin, globulins and fibrinogen; it also contains salts, nutrients, hormones, gases and waste products.
Plasma transports these substances around the body, and fibrinogen helps in blood clotting.

items.followUp: What is animal breeding, and how is it useful in animal husbandry?

rubric.why: Identifies the activity as the care and rearing of animals.
rubric.description: Animal husbandry is the care and rearing of domestic animals.
rubric.how: Award for describing the rearing or management of animals.

rubric.why: States the purpose or products of animal husbandry.
rubric.description: It is carried out to obtain useful products such as milk, meat, eggs, wool or hides.
rubric.how: Award for stating a useful purpose or a suitable animal product.

modelAnswer: Animal husbandry is the care, management and rearing of domestic animals.
It is practised to obtain useful products such as milk, meat, eggs, wool and hides.

rubric.why: Checks the definition and subject of histology.
rubric.description: Histology is the scientific study of tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a study and 1 mark for naming tissues as its subject.

modelAnswer: Histology is the scientific study of tissues.

items.followUp: In an investigation, what is the difference between an independent variable and a dependent variable?

rubric.why: Describes the control group as the baseline without the tested treatment or factor.
rubric.description: The control group does not receive the experimental treatment and provides a basis for comparison.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the control group lacks the tested treatment/factor or serves as the comparison.

rubric.why: Describes the experimental group as receiving the tested treatment or factor.
rubric.description: The experimental group receives the treatment or is exposed to the factor being tested.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the experimental group receives the tested treatment/factor.

modelAnswer: The control group does not receive the experimental treatment and provides a basis for comparison.
The experimental group receives the treatment or is exposed to the factor being tested.
